entries.text: Conceitedness in one's own wisdom reproved. Prov. 3:7; Prov. 26:5; Isa. 5:21; Rom, 11:20,25;
Wealth produces conceited thoughts.
Beware of those who are lovers of themselves.
God does not take account of self-righteousness.
Self-righteousness condemned.
Do not glory or trust in your riches.
You are not to trust in the abundance of your riches, for he who trusts in his riches will fall.
The wicked boasts of his heart's desires.
Not he who commends himself is approved, but he whom the Lord commends.
Do not practice your righteousness or give alms (food, clothes, money, etc. given to the poor) before men so as to draw attention to your deed of mercy, otherwise you have no reward with God.
Do not boast about tomorrow, for you know not what a day may bring forth.
Do not go about to establish your own righteousness, but submit yourselves to the righteousness of God.
All boasting and bragging is wicked.
We are not to justify ourselves.
We should not believe in our own righteousness.
Self-righteousness provokes God to anger.
The boastful shall not stand in God's sight.
To seek one's own glory is not glory.
Let another man praise you, and not your own mouth, a stranger, and not your own lips.
Do not be wise in your own eyes or prudent in your own sight.
The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, but he who heeds counsel is wise.
